newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.85/86 vs dlr in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.85/86 vs dlr in dull trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.85/86 against the dollar on Thursday, unchanged from the day's opening rate in lacklustre trade, dealers said.

"It was absolutely dull," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay. He said demand for dollars from some city banks pulled the rupee to 35.86/87 in the early session, but the rupee soon sprang back to the 35.85/86 level.
The forward dollar saw two-way movement on account of profit-taking and paying pressure from some banks, dealers said.
The six-month premium closed the day at 7.42 percent, up from the previous close of 7.36 percent, dealers said.
"The rupee needs to fall to 37.7 against the dollar by March 1997 to maintain its real exchange fair value," securities firm SocGen-Crosby said in a research report on Thursday.
But the extent of depreciation will be determined by the Reserve Bank of India, dealers said.
